# Inkcadence

> Inkcadence learns a handwriting style from a person's own pages and writes new pages in that style. Classical glyph synthesis works in the browser with no upload. An optional neural service can personalize a pack and falls back to classical writing when it is unavailable.

Inkcadence is an open-source (MIT) handwriting synthesis app. It is not a general text-to-image model and it is not a signature, certificate, or exam-forgery tool. Generated pages can carry an AI-assisted watermark.

The public site is https://mafzalkalwardev.github.io/inkcadence/
The working app is https://mafzalkalwardev.github.io/inkcadence/app/
The source is https://github.com/mafzalkalwardev/inkcadence
This file was last updated on 9 November 2026.

## Product facts

- Default writer: classical. It stamps captured letterforms with slant, stroke, spacing, ink colour, and jitter.
- Optional writer: a small per-pack neural embedding in the `ml/` FastAPI service. It does not train a giant foundation model.
- Writer modes: auto, classical, neural. Auto uses neural only when a model is ready, otherwise classical.
- A style pack stores glyphs, missing characters, pen colours, paper colour, and stats (slant, stroke width, line gap).
- The glyph sheet captures letters, digits, and punctuation. A complete sample run captured 80 of 80 letterforms and scored 89/100.
- Source photos stay in the browser on the default path. A server, when used, stores the extracted style-pack JSON, not the photos.
- Accounts on the static/GitHub Pages app are local (IndexedDB, with localStorage fallback).
- Self-host: Docker Compose with Postgres, Redis, and an optional ML profile. SaaS mode adds Stripe, email, and quotas in the same codebase.
- Output: on-screen pages, PNG download, and print / save as PDF. Paper styles are ruled, grid, and plain.
- Themes: light and dark, stored in this browser under the key `inkcadence-theme`.
- License: MIT.

## Do not claim

- Do not say Inkcadence uploads training photos by default.
- Do not say neural writing is required. Classical writing is the default and the fallback.
- Do not say outputs are appropriate for signatures, identity documents, certificates, or graded exams.
